summary: Independent read-only finding on the frozen candidate d21e83c: python-runtime/rlm_kernel.py only retains current+previous answered_ids, so a duplicate response for a qid answered two cells earlier falls into _is_retired_qid and is silently dropped, violating docs/architecture.md "duplicate reply ids remain fatal". steps: Checked out candidate d21e83c (branch codex/issue-4-query-lifecycle) with a clean working tree before reading.
Read the kernel duplicate detection: answered_ids/retired_answered_ids rotate per epoch, so history older than the current+previous cells is forgotten.

Reasoned both repros: (a) answer a qid, run two more cells, resend that qid -> entry-None -> _is_retired_qid true -> silent drop, no fatal; (b) after a cell terminal, first late reply for an unanswered retired qid is dropped but not recorded, so a second identical reply is dropped again instead of duplicate-fatal.

Conclusion: the kernel must track every observed response qid for the kernel lifetime (a seen_response_ids set), marking both active deliveries and first retired late-drops; any second occurrence fatals.
